Reasoning was mixed, some found it easy while others considered it moderate, and math was seen as the toughest section with many advanced topics and time pressure. GK was mostly static and English passages were lengthy but manageable.

intro: The SSC CGL Tier 1 exam held on 8 October 2026 was conducted in three shifts. Shift 1 and Shift 2 have full reports, while Shift 3 is only partially reported and will be updated once complete. Most analysts rated Shift 1 as Easy to Moderate, with good attempts ranging between 70 and 90 questions. Shift 2 showed mixed difficulty across sections, with good attempts reported between 22 and 89. Figures presented are unofficial and SSC normalises scores across shifts.

faqs.q: What was the overall difficulty level of the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam on 8 October 2026?
faqs.a: Shift 1 and Shift 2 were both described as Easy to Moderate overall, while Shift 3 was reported as Easy by the limited data available.

faqs.q: How many questions did candidates attempt well in each shift of the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 on 8 October 2026?
faqs.a: Shift 1 had good attempts between 70 and 90 questions, Shift 2 reported a broader range of 22 to 89 questions, and Shift 3 showed a single reported figure of 87 good attempts.

faqs.q: Which sections were reported as most challenging in the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 on 8 October 2026?
faqs.a: Quantitative Aptitude was noted as the toughest in Shift 1 and ranged from moderate to difficult in Shift 2; Reasoning and General Awareness also showed mixed difficulty across the shifts.

faqs.q: Are the attempt figures for the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 on 8 October 2026 official?
faqs.a: No, the figures are unofficial; SSC normally normalises scores across shifts before publishing official statistics.

faqs.q: When will the analysis for any pending shift of the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 on 8 October 2026 be added?
faqs.a: The analysis for Shift 3, which is currently partial, will be added after the shift’s full data becomes available.
